---
name: Findings from testing CompileML
about: You put the library through its paces and want to report what you found
labels: documentation
---

**What you tested it against.** Data shape, base rate, which teacher, which
parts of the library.

**What worked.** Genuinely useful — it tells us which claims survive contact
with data we do not have, and confirmed behaviour is as informative as a bug.

**What did not.** Rough notes are fine. A list of observations is more
welcome than nothing, and far more welcome than a polished report that never
gets written. If it turns out some are bugs, we will split them into their
own issues and credit you.

**Anything that was merely confusing.** A warning that says the wrong thing,
a default that surprised you, a function whose docstring did not match what
it did. These matter as much as defects, and they are the things a
maintainer cannot see from the inside.

---

You are welcome to write this up wherever suits you and just link it here —
an issue, a gist, a repository of your own. The point is that it reaches us,
not that it arrives in any particular shape.
